inbounds.title: Inbounds
inbounds.subtitle: Where the core accepts its users
inbounds.noCertificate: Add a certificate on the Certificates page first
inbounds.targetHint: The site connections look like; it needs TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2
inbounds.sniffingHint: Reads the real domain from HTTP, TLS and QUIC for better routing
inbounds.deleteBody: “{{name}}” and its hosts are deleted and its connections end.
inbounds.empty: No inbound yet. The core starts with the first one.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.subtitle: TLS certificates for the panel and its inbounds; get them from an authority and they renew themselves
certificates.name: Name
certificates.empty: No certificates yet. Get a free one, make a self-signed one, or upload your own.
certificates.issueTitle: Get a certificate from an authority
certificates.issueBody: Each name is proven with a challenge, and the certificate is kept here and renewed before it expires.
certificates.namesHint: One per line or comma-separated: a domain, *.domain (wildcard) or an IP address
certificates.method: How to prove the names are yours
certificates.methodAutoHint: Port 80 if it is free, else the TLS port; with a wildcard, every name is proven with DNS.
certificates.methodHttpHint: The authority comes to port 80 of this server from the internet; it must be open and free.
certificates.methodTlsHint: The authority connects to port 443 of this server; if the panel is on that port it answers there.
certificates.methodDnsHint: A TXT record is written at Cloudflare and removed again; for a domain behind a CDN, and for wildcards.
certificates.needCloudflare: DNS and wildcards need a Cloudflare token: set one in “Issuing settings”.
certificates.autoRenewHint: It renews itself before it expires, and the panel and inbounds take the new one without a break.
certificates.issuing: Getting the certificate… it takes up to two minutes; keep this page open.
certificates.selfSignedBody: For where no authority's certificate will do. Clients do not trust it unless told to. It does not renew and is valid for five years.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.subtitle: Addresses users reach each inbound by (for links and subscriptions)
hosts.portHint: Empty means the inbound's own port
hosts.allowInsecureHint: For testing only; it removes the connection's security
hosts.empty: No host yet. Without one, links use the server's address.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Each user reaches inbounds through its groups, and the panel holds it to its limits.
users.namesLike: {{first}} to {{last}}; names already taken are skipped.
users.onHoldHint: Its time starts on its first connection.
users.onHoldDaysHint: Its first connection sets the expiry this far ahead.
users.onHoldTimeoutHint: If it never connects by then, its time starts on its own.
users.groupsHint: The user reaches the inbounds its groups give.
users.ipLimitHint: Addresses that came last are cut off.
users.holdFor_one: {{count, number}} day after its first connection
users.holdFor_other: {{count, number}} days after its first connection
users.revokeBody: {{name}} gets a new UUID, password and subscription link, and its open sessions end. Its old config stops working.
users.deleteBody: {{name}} is deleted for good and its sessions end.
users.empty: No users yet. Create the first one.
users.nextPlanHint: When the user runs out of data or time, it moves on to this plan instead of being cut off (once).
users.carryOverHint: Data left of the old limit is added to the new one.
users.setGroupsHint: The selected users end up in exactly these groups.
users.bulkResetBody_one: This period's usage of {{count, number}} user goes back to zero.
users.bulkResetBody_other: This period's usage of {{count, number}} users goes back to zero.
users.bulkRevokeBody_one: {{count, number}} user gets new credentials; its old config stops working.
users.bulkRevokeBody_other: {{count, number}} users get new credentials; their old configs stop working.
users.bulkDeleteBody_one: {{count, number}} user is deleted for good.
users.bulkDeleteBody_other: {{count, number}} users are deleted for good.
users.hwidLimitHint: Devices the subscription may be fetched on (from the app's x-hwid header). Blank means any.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: A group gives access to some inbounds; its users get all of them.
groups.name: Name
groups.allInboundsHint: Inbounds made later are included too.
groups.deleteBody_one: {{name}} is deleted, and its {{count, number}} user loses the access it gave.
groups.deleteBody_other: {{name}} is deleted, and its {{count, number}} users lose the access it gave them.

templates.name: Name
templates.onHoldHint: Users are made on hold, and their days count from their first connection.
templates.groupsHint: Blank keeps the groups picked in the user form.
templates.deleteBody: {{name}} is deleted; users made with it stay as they are.

subscription.urlHint: Put this link in the user's app; its configs and usage stay up to date on their own.
subscription.localWarning: This link starts with an address only this computer (or its network) can reach, because the panel was opened that way. It will not work for anyone else. Open the panel by its real address or domain, or set the public address under Settings → Subscription.
subscription.noConfigs: No configs: the user is not active, or its groups give no inbound.
subscription.neverFetched: The subscription has not been fetched yet.
subscription.settingsBody: Users' subscription links, and what apps show from them.
subscription.publicUrlHint: The address links are made with; blank for the one the panel is opened at.
subscription.serverAddressHint: For inbounds without a host; blank for the name the app fetched the subscription by.
subscription.hwidRequired: Only apps that send a device id
subscription.hwidRequiredHint: For a user with a device limit, an app that sends no x-hwid is refused.
subscription.templateHint: Your own HTML for browsers; {{data}} becomes the subscription as JSON. Blank for the built-in page.
subscription.legacyPathHint: Where 3X-UI gave out this format (/json, /clash): the links users already have keep working. Empty for none.

core.title: Core settings
core.subtitle: Outbounds, routing, DNS and zray's own features; every change is checked first and stored only if the core accepts it.
core.proposedBar: The preset is loaded in the editor; review it and apply.
core.nothingToApply: Everything is as the core has it now.
core.applied_restarted: Applied; the ports changed over without a gap.
core.applied_stopped: Saved; no inbound is on, so the core is stopped.
core.tagHint: The name rules refer to it by.
core.outboundsBody: The ways users' traffic reaches the internet. The first outbound takes whatever no rule sends elsewhere.
core.linkHint: A vless, vmess, trojan, ss, hysteria2 or tuic link, or warp://. Copy it from another app or server.
core.warpHint: The WARP account's keys are made on this server and only their public halves go to Cloudflare. The server must be able to reach Cloudflare's API.
core.dialThroughHint: The connection to this outbound's server goes out through another outbound, such as WARP: a proxy chain.
core.fragmentHint: Hides the site name from the filter; only for TLS and Reality outbounds.
core.allowInsecureHint: For tests only; it leaves the connection open to interception.
core.domainStrategyHint: AsIs hands the name to the destination as it is; UseIP resolves it first.
core.blackholeHint: Whatever reaches this outbound is dropped without a word; for blocking destinations by rule.
core.torHint: Traffic goes through Tor. The core must be built with Tor support.
core.jsonOutboundHint: Write any Xray or zray outbound as it is.
core.deleteOutboundBody: {{tag}} is removed from the editor; Apply sends it to the core.
core.deleteOutboundUsed: {{tag}} is still named by {{uses}}. If you delete it, the core's check will refuse until you fix those.
core.deleteLastOutbound: This is the only outbound. The core refuses settings without one.
core.routingBody: Rules are tried in order, and the first that matches sends the traffic.
core.routingStrategy_IPIfNonMatch: IPIfNonMatch (the IP if no rule matched the name)
core.routingStrategy_IPOnDemand: IPOnDemand (whenever an IP rule needs it)
core.routingStrategyHint: For geoip rules on traffic that arrives with a name, pick one of the IP modes.
core.blockPrivateHint: Users cannot reach the server's loopback, internal network and link-local addresses, so they cannot get at services that trust the server itself. This rule always runs first.
core.rulesBody: A rule has some conditions that must all hold; within a list, one entry is enough.
core.noRules: No rules: all traffic goes to the default outbound.
core.ruleHint: A blank condition means anything. Give at least one condition unless this is the last, catch-all rule.
core.ruleMatchesAll: With no condition this rule takes all the traffic, and the rules after it never run.
core.ruleDomainHint: One per line: domain:, full:, keyword:, regexp: or geosite:.
core.ruleIpHint: An address, a CIDR range or geoip:, one per line.
core.ruleUsersHint: Usernames; the rule only applies to these users.
core.deleteRuleBody: Rule number {{number, number}} is removed from the editor.
core.balancersBody: Makes several outbounds one: traffic is spread among them or goes to the best. A rule can point at a balancer.
core.balancerSelectorHint: One tag or tag prefix per line; every outbound starting with it is chosen.
core.strategyNeedsObservatory: It needs the observatory to measure the outbounds.
core.deleteBalancerBody: Balancer {{tag}} is removed from the editor.
core.observatoryBody: Every so often fetches an address through each outbound, so the least-ping and least-load balancers know which is better.
core.observatorySubjectsHint: One tag or tag prefix per line.
core.geodataBody: Rules like geosite:category-ir and geoip:ir need these lists; a tag that is not in them matches nothing.
core.geodataManage: Keep the lists up to date
core.geodataManageHint: The core downloads them from several mirrors and refreshes them daily.
core.geodataTags: {{sites, number}} geosite tags and {{ips, number}} geoip tags loaded
core.geodataApplyFirst: Once the settings are applied, the download status shows here.
core.dnsBody: How the names users ask for are found.
core.queryStrategyHint: If the server has no IPv6, IPv4 only saves pointless attempts.
core.leakPolicyHint: On a server that sends traffic out directly, its own resolver is the right one. With any proxy outbound the core forbids it itself, since it would answer outside the tunnel.
core.dnsDisableCacheHint: Every query is asked afresh; slower.
core.dnsServersBody: Asked in order. A resolver with a list of domains only answers for those.
core.noDnsServers: No resolvers; without one no name is found.
core.dnsAddressHint: An IP, or https://… (DoH), tls://… (DoT), quic://… (DoQ), or localhost for the server's own resolver.
core.dnsExpect: The answer must be in these IPs
core.dnsExpectHint: An answer outside them is dropped and the next resolver is asked.
core.dnsTagHint: To name this resolver from a rule (directVia).
core.dnsSkipFallback: Leave out of the fallback chain
core.dnsSkipFallbackHint: If it gives no answer, the next resolver is not tried.
core.deleteDnsServerBody: This resolver is removed from the editor.
core.dnsHostsBody: A name that gets a fixed answer without asking anyone.
core.dnsHostsLabel: One per line: a name and its answer
core.dnsHostsHint: Separate several IPs with commas; an answer of #block blocks the name.
core.presetCardBody: A ready-made set for the Iranian network: three DNS tiers (anti-sanction, domestic, encrypted), routing of Iranian domains and IPs, ad blocking and the geodata lists. It replaces the panel's current outbounds and rules.
core.presetBody: The proposed settings are loaded in the editor and not yet on the core; you can look, edit, and then apply.
core.presetLinksHint: One link per line. The first takes whatever no rule sends elsewhere.
core.fragmentBody: For each TLS or Reality outbound, choose whether its first hello is split in pieces.
core.cleanIpBody: Among several Cloudflare edge addresses, finds the one that works on this network and points the CDN-fronted outbounds at it.
core.jsonBody: All the settings but the inbounds (which have their own page). The blockPrivate key is the panel's own; the rest is the core's JSON.
core.geodataNeeded: Your rules or DNS name geosite or geoip tags, but no lists are loaded; those tags match nothing.
core.dnsForcedStrict: An outbound sends traffic through another server; then the core never uses the server's own resolver, whatever the system-resolver setting says.
core.dnsNoResolver: You now have only the system resolver, so no name resolves, for direct connections either. Add a resolver by address (DoH, DoT or UDP) or use the Iran preset.

forbidden.title: No access
forbidden.body: Your admin may not open this page. If you need it, ask a sudo admin to change your role.

access.title: Admins and access
access.subtitle: Admins, roles, and what each may see and change; resellers see only the users they made.
access.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the current one. A new password signs the admin out everywhere.
access.sudoHint: A sudo admin sees everything and manages admins and roles. Give it only to people you trust.
access.roleHint: The role sets what they may do; the quotas and allowed groups below are for this admin alone.
access.dataQuotaHint: The total data they may hand out to their users. 0 means no cap; with a quota, users must have a data limit.
access.groupsHint: The groups they may give their users; none ticked means all.
access.enabledHint: A disabled admin cannot sign in and their API keys stop working; their users stay connected.
access.selfHint: You cannot turn yourself off or change your own role; ask another sudo admin.
access.unlimitedUsers_one: {{count, number}} user without a data limit
access.unlimitedUsers_other: {{count, number}} users without a data limit
access.deleteBody_one: They own {{count, number}} user, and their API keys are deleted too. The user is not deleted: it goes to the admin you pick.
access.deleteBody_other: They own {{count, number}} users, and their API keys are deleted too. The users are not deleted: they go to the admin you pick.
access.ownUsersHint: An admin with this role sees and changes only the users they made (a reseller).
access.permissionsHint: “View” only shows; “Manage” also allows changes. Managing admins and roles is for sudo admins alone.
access.deleteRoleUsed_one: {{count, number}} admin has the role “{{name}}”; change theirs first.
access.deleteRoleUsed_other: {{count, number}} admins have the role “{{name}}”; change theirs first.
access.quotaUnlimitedWarn: Some of your users have no data limit, which a quota cannot count.

developer.title: API
developer.subtitle: The panel can be run from scripts and bots too: everything the dashboard does.
developer.keysBody: An API key is like an admin's password for scripts: it works with the permissions you give it and from the addresses you name. The whole key is shown only once.
developer.noKeyAccess: Your admin may not make API keys.
developer.noKeys: You have not made a key yet.
developer.keyNameHint: To tell it apart, such as “Telegram bot”.
developer.scopeHint_read: Only to view every part you can view yourself; it changes nothing.
developer.scopeHint_custom: Set each part on its own; never more than you may do yourself.
developer.scopeHint_full: Anything you can do. For tools you trust.
developer.allowedIpsHint: One address or range per line (such as 10.0.0.0/8). Empty means from anywhere.
developer.revokeBody: The key “{{name}}” stops working at once, and this cannot be undone.
developer.keyMadeBody: Copy it now: the panel keeps only a hash of it and will not show it again.
developer.realCall: This call really runs and changes things.
developer.streamNote: This is a live stream; try it with cURL or EventSource.

notify.title: Notifications & bot
notify.subtitle: Telegram, Discord and webhooks: what is told, to whom, and how.
notify.generalBody: The language of messages, and the proxy deliveries go through.
notify.proxyHint: If Telegram or Discord is blocked from your server: http://host:port or socks5://host:port (with user:pass@ if it asks), such as the core's own SOCKS inbound. Empty goes direct.
notify.telegramBody: A bot for admins (figures, search and managing users from a chat) and for users (usage and link), and notifications to chats and channels. It listens by long polling and needs no public address.
notify.tokenHint: From @BotFather. Entered once and never shown again.
notify.secretSet: Saved; leave empty to keep it
notify.apiBaseHint: https://api.telegram.org by default; put a relay of it here if you use one.
notify.chats: Chats and channels that hear everything
notify.chatsHint: Numeric ids, one a line or separated by commas. A channel's id starts with -100. Send /id to the bot to see a chat's. Admins who tied their chat get notifications on their own.
notify.userBotHint: A user sends the bot their subscription link and sees their own usage.
notify.notifyUsersHint: When their own data or time is running out, or has run out.
notify.discordBody: Notifications in a channel, through an incoming webhook. (The bot's commands are Telegram only.)
notify.webhookBody: Each notification is POSTed to your address as JSON. With a secret, every request is signed (HMAC-SHA256, in the X-Z-UI-Signature header) so you can check it came from this panel.
notify.webhookSecretHint: Optional; the key of the signature.
notify.eventsBody: Each thing is told once. When this is first switched on, old cases are not announced.
notify.event_data_lowHint: To the admins and (if on) the user.
notify.event_expiringHint: A few days before a user's subscription ends.
notify.event_limitedHint: When a user reaches its data limit.
notify.event_coreHint: It stops while an inbound is enabled, and when it is running again.
notify.event_login_failedHint: Several wrong passwords in a row, or an address locked out.
notify.event_login_newHint: An admin signs in from an address they had not before.
notify.dataLowPercentHint: When this share of a user's data is used.
notify.expiringDaysHint: When this many days are left of a subscription.
notify.saveFirst: The test uses what is saved; save first.
notify.event_certificateHint: Renewed, could not be renewed, or one that does not renew itself is about to expire.
notify.event_updateHint: A newer version of Z-UI is published.
notify.serverBody: Tell me when the server is under strain, when the traffic reaches another step, and when the machine restarts. Each is told once, and again when it is back to normal.
notify.tempHint: Only where the server has a sensor; most virtual servers have none, and then nothing is told.
notify.trafficHint: All the traffic the panel has carried, told each time it passes another multiple of the step.
notify.reliefBody: When the processor or the temperature stays over its limit (the numbers above), the panel can step in: users who are connected but idle leave for a few minutes, and the busiest users are held to a modest speed until the load is down. Everything it does is undone by itself, and you are told when it starts and stops.
notify.reliefOn: Step in when the server is strained
notify.reliefOnHint: Off by default: slowing users is a choice only you can make.
notify.reliefPause: Send idle users out for a while
notify.reliefPauseHint: Connected but moved nothing for the idle time; they leave the core and come back by themselves.
notify.reliefThrottleHint: The users that moved the most lately are held to the speed below until things calm down.
notify.reliefMaxHint: Whatever it did is lifted after this long, strained or not.

telegramLink.title: My Telegram
telegramLink.body: Tie your private chat to this account so the bot does for you what you may do, and sends your notifications.
telegramLink.send: Send this to the bot in a private chat:
telegramLink.expires: The code is good for {{minutes, number}} minutes, once.
telegramLink.off: The Telegram bot is not on; a sudo admin turns it on under Notifications & bot.

backup.title: Backup
backup.subtitle: A whole copy of what the panel keeps, and putting it back.
backup.nowBody: Users, inbounds, admins, certificates and settings. Kept in the data directory, and sent to Telegram if that is on.
backup.never: No backup has been made yet.
backup.filesBody: The last {{keep, number}} are kept. The files hold every secret of the panel; keep them somewhere safe.
backup.scheduleBody: Automatic backups, where they go and how they are protected.
backup.toTelegramHint: To the listed chats and the sudo admins' chats, up to 50 MB.
backup.usageHint: Large; the panel works fully without it, and each user's total stays in the user.
backup.passphraseHint: Optional. Seals the file (XChaCha20-Poly1305); without it the file cannot be put back, so do not lose it. At least 8 characters.
backup.restoreBody: Everything the panel holds is replaced by what a backup file holds. What it holds now is first saved as a file of its own.
backup.confirm1: All current users, inbounds, admins and settings are replaced by those in the backup.
backup.confirm2: Everyone is signed out; the admins are those the backup had.
backup.confirm3: A copy of what the panel holds now stays in the backups, so you can go back.
backup.restoredBody: The panel is now as it was on {{when}}. Sign in again.

acme.title: Issuing settings
acme.subtitle: Which authority, with which email, and on which ports the challenges are answered.
acme.ca_letsencrypt_staging: Let's Encrypt · staging (its certificates are not trusted, its limits are loose)
acme.emailHint: The authority writes here before a certificate expires. ZeroSSL needs one.
acme.eabHint: ZeroSSL and some others give accounts only with a key. For ZeroSSL, leave empty and it is fetched with the email.
acme.cloudflareHint: Only for DNS challenges and wildcards; the permission Zone → DNS → Edit is enough. It is not shown again once saved.
acme.httpPortHint: The authority always asks on port 80: change this only if that is forwarded to it.
acme.renewDaysHint: A short-lived certificate (for an IP) starts at a third of its life.
acme.dnsWait: Wait after writing a DNS record (seconds)
acme.proxy: Proxy for the authority and Cloudflare
acme.proxyHint: http://… or socks5://…; empty is direct.

panelAccess.title: Panel address and HTTPS
panelAccess.body: The port, the secret path and the HTTPS certificate of the panel itself. The address and path apply after a restart.
panelAccess.listenHint: Like 0.0.0.0:2053; with 127.0.0.1 it is only seen behind a proxy.
panelAccess.pathHint: The panel answers only under this path, and anywhere else is a 404.
panelAccess.certificateHint: Get a certificate on the Certificates page. Swapping it for another applies at once; going from HTTP to HTTPS or back needs a restart.
panelAccess.locked: Fixed by a flag or a ZUI_* variable; it cannot be changed here.
panelAccess.restartNeeded: Saved. It applies after a restart.
panelAccess.restartBody: The panel is out of reach for a few seconds, then opens at the new address. If the path changes, or you go from HTTPS to HTTP, you sign in again.
panelAccess.restarting: The panel is starting again… in a few seconds you are taken to the new address.
panelAccess.warning: A wrong address or path puts the panel out of reach; on the server, z-ui setting reset puts everything back to the defaults.

update.title: Updates
update.body: Get the panel's newer version from its releases. Every release is signed, and the panel takes only one that carries the maintainers' signature.
update.upToDate: This is the newest version (last looked {{when}}).
update.container: This panel runs in a container; it is updated by pulling a new image, not from here.
update.cannotApply: The program's directory cannot be written, so the panel cannot replace itself; update from the server with z-ui update apply.
update.applyBody: The new version is downloaded and its signature checked, it is started once to see that it is right, and then it takes the place of this one (which is kept). The panel is out of reach for a few seconds.
update.restarting: The new version is in place and the panel is starting again… the page opens in a few seconds.
update.checkHint: Looks every few hours and says in Notifications when there is something new.
update.proxyHint: If GitHub is closed from your server: http://… or socks5://…; empty is direct.

migrate.title: Migration
migrate.subtitle: Bring the users, inbounds and quota of 3X-UI, PasarGuard or Marzban over; the subscription links already handed out keep working.
migrate.uploadBody: Upload the database file of the panel you are leaving. It is read and shown to you first; nothing changes until you confirm.
migrate.notADatabase: This does not look like a database file.
migrate.kindHint: Found out from the file; say it only if it guessed wrong.
migrate.previewBody: A {{size}} file. Nothing has been written here yet.
migrate.needsConfig: Marzban keeps its inbounds in a file beside the database, not in it. Give xray_config.json too, or the users come without inbounds.

links.tokens: Every user keeps its subscription token, so the links already handed out keep working at the same address: set the same subscription path (and domain) under Settings.
links.signed: The links the old panel signed keep working: they are checked with its key, which is kept here. A user whose credentials are revoked here loses its old link as well.

warning.renamed: {{name}} is renamed to be a valid name or tag here.
warning.unsupported_protocol: {{name}} is of a kind this panel does not build, so it is not imported (VLESS, VMess, Trojan and Shadowsocks are).
warning.remote_inbound: {{name}} runs on another node of the old panel, not on this server, so it is not imported.
warning.inbound_limit_ignored: {{name}} had a limit on the whole inbound; that is not imported, users have their own.
warning.client_without_email: An account on {{name}} has no email, which is its name here, so it is left out.
warning.flow_for_all: VLESS flow is the inbound's here, not each user's: the commonest one is set for everyone on the inbound.
warning.method_set: {{name}}: its users each had a Shadowsocks method; the inbound uses the commonest for all.
warning.credentials_changed: Some users had one id (or password) for one protocol and another for another. Here a user has one of each kind; the saved configs of the other protocol stop working until they fetch the subscription again.
warning.different_ids: {{name}} had a different id on different inbounds; one is kept, and its subscription gives the rest.
warning.shared_sub_id: {{name}} shared its subscription link with another user; the first keeps it and this one gets a new one.
warning.no_inbound: {{name}} was only on inbounds that are not imported, so it has no access yet.
warning.id_not_uuid: {{name}} had an id that is not a UUID, so a new one is made.
warning.reset_approximated: {{name}} reset every few days; here the nearest period is used (day, week, month or year).
warning.core_not_imported: {{name}} is a core other than Xray; it is not imported.
warning.core_unreadable: {{name}} has a configuration that cannot be read as JSON.
warning.host_without_inbound: {{name}} is a host of no inbound.
warning.host_first_only: {{name}} listed several SNI or Host names; the first is kept.
warning.host_security_ignored: {{name}} overrides the inbound's security (TLS); that is not imported, the inbound's own applies.
warning.host_features_ignored: {{name}} uses features hosts do not have here (fragment, noise, mux, extra headers); they are not imported.
warning.no_xray_config: Marzban's inbounds are in xray_config.json, which was not given: users, hosts and templates come, but no inbounds and no access groups.
warning.group_disabled: {{name}} was disabled there, so here it holds no inbounds.
warning.skipped_exists: {{name}} is already here, so it is left out.
warning.skipped_invalid: {{name}} has a port that is not between 1 and 65535, so it is left out.
warning.skipped_protocol: {{name}} is of a kind this panel does not build, so it is left out.
warning.skipped_core: {{name}} was refused by the core's own check (see the details), so it is left out.
warning.skipped_error: {{name}} could not be added (see the details).
warning.cert_not_taken: The certificate of {{name}} could not be brought into the store; it keeps naming its files.
warning.old_links_not_kept: The old panel's signed links cannot be kept (see the details).
warning.subscription_settings_refused: The old panel's subscription settings were not taken (see the details).
warning.no_sudo_admin: None of the admins was an owner, so the first became a sudo admin here.

opt.users: Users, with quota, dates and credentials
opt.settingsHint: The old panel's path, title and update interval.
opt.enableHint: Off, they come in switched off: the old panel still holds their ports until it is stopped. Switch them on under Inbounds when it has been.
opt.conflictHint: A user or template named like one that is already here.
opt.adminsHint: Each gets a link to set a password; a user stays its admin's.

migrate.confirm1: A backup of everything this panel holds is made first; restoring it under Backup undoes the import.
migrate.confirm2: Users, inbounds and groups are added to what is here; nothing here is deleted or replaced.
migrate.confirm3: Nothing is changed in the old panel.
migrate.coreError: The core did not take the new configuration: {{message}}
migrate.next1: Look through the users and the groups they are in.
migrate.next2: Stop the old panel, then switch the inbounds on under Inbounds.
migrate.next3: Make the subscription domain and path what users already have, under Settings.

takeover.title: {{panel}} was replaced by this panel
takeover.body: {{users}} users and {{inbounds}} inbounds came over, and users' apps reconnected by themselves. The old panel's files stay where they are, stopped, until {{date}} ({{left}}), so you can go back.
takeover.back: I made a mistake: bring the old panel back
takeover.cannotBack: The old panel's files are not where they were, so there is nothing to go back to.
takeover.back1: This panel stops, and {{panel}} starts again with its own files.
takeover.back2: Everything its users used while this panel served is added to {{panel}}'s own counters, so nothing is lost.
takeover.back3: Users made here since are not in {{panel}}, and settings changed here are not carried back.
takeover.back4: You will be cut off from this panel: afterwards open {{panel}} at its own address.
takeover.started: Going back has started. This panel stops in a moment; {{panel}} starts at its own address.
takeover.deleteBody: They are deleted for good, and there is no way back to {{panel}} after this. They would be deleted by themselves on {{date}} anyway.
takeover.deleted: The files of {{panel}} were deleted on {{when}}; there is no way back.
takeover.rolledBack: {{panel}} was brought back on {{when}}. This panel does not start by itself.
takeover.prepared: A takeover of {{panel}} was prepared but has not switched yet; it is switched from the server.
takeover.bannerBody: This panel replaced {{panel}} on {{when}}. If something is wrong you can still go back ({{left}}).
